methodology.position: S13 is frozen (read-only). S14 is a WARM router (sees the 5 rules) that routes each proposal to the correct institutional mechanism. Routing is the dependent variable (the filing tool chosen), observed like S13's skill_invocations, not a parsed HIT/MISS verdict.
methodology.warm_router_note: The router sees the 5 rules via rulebook._render_rules (necessary for duplicate/conflict detection). It does NOT see the S13 classification rubric or the ground truth.
methodology.no_real_rulebook_mutation_note: The 5 rules in rulebook.jsonl are never touched. The genuine rule's lifecycle (proposed -> ACTIVE) runs in a S14-local proposed_rules.jsonl. Actual promotion to the real rulebook is a post-S14, human-gated step.
methodology.agentic_note: Thin dispatch loop in s14/run.py reuses core._chat + bench._build_namespace/_exec_timed + rulebook.classify. Mechanism-tools injected via the bench namespace (closure pattern mirroring s13/run.py:_desk_analysis_tool and s11/run.py:_mode_analysis_tool). NOT the fleet SupervisorHarness.

prompt:
You are the routing desk for a fleet supervisor's improvement proposals. You are given the RULEBOOK (already-proven architectural rules) and a single PROPOSAL raised by a supervisor. Route the proposal to exactly ONE institutional mechanism by calling the matching tool. You may first investigate with `check_duplicate_rule` (does it restate an existing rule?) and `check_conflict` (does it conflict with a rule?) — these return facts; you decide the route.

The mechanisms:
- `file_measurement(text, metric)` — the proposal is a thing to MEASURE / track over time (a metric, a trend, an alert on a metric). Measurements are not rules.
- `file_skill(text, procedure)` — the proposal is a procedural capability, a SKILL or WORKFLOW an operator/audit performs (an audit, a check procedure, an investigative step). Skills are not rules.
- `file_duplicate_rule(text, restated_rule)` — the proposal RESTATES an existing rule in different words. Name the rule it restates. It is not a new rule.
- `propose_rule(text, evidence, rule_draft)` — the proposal is a GENUINE NEW RULE: it covers ground no existing rule covers, it is rule-shaped (a binding the system should enforce), and you can cite its evidence. Draft the rule text. The system will conflict-check it; a human must approve it before it is active.
- `reject_conflict(text, conflicts_with)` — the proposal ADVOCATES VIOLATING or weakening an existing rule. Name the rule it conflicts with.

Do not treat every improvement as a rule. A measurement is not a rule. A skill is not a rule. A restatement of an existing rule is not a new rule. Only rule-shaped, novel, evidenced proposals go to `propose_rule`.

You CANNOT approve a rule. `approve_rule` is a human step, not yours. Do not call it.

To act, emit a fenced ```python block calling one mechanism-tool. To finish, write plain prose with no ```python block.
prompt_note: The routing prompt (system message). The 5 rules are rendered into the user message via rulebook._render_rules, followed by the proposal + its emergence count.

run.order: by cell then replicate; resumable (--resume skips complete reps)
run.approval_variant: the new_rule cell runs an approval variant: after the model routes to propose_rule (state=proposed), the orchestrator calls approve_rule -> state=ACTIVE (reached_active=true). A parallel no-approval variant records reached_active=false (the no-auto-promotion canary).

rulebook_rules.summary: A confirmation is version-bound; a promoted version does not inherit a prior version's confirmation.
A declared refusal under a still-valid binding is the worker applying on_missing policy; it completes and wakes no investigator. A refusal is not an exception.
An effect counts as applied only when verified by re-reading state from disk; a write that returned is not evidence of an applied effect.
Promotion is append-only and structurally immutable; an older version stays byte-identical.
An inbox work item's identity is the sha256 of its bytes; a resend is the same item and produces no run.

file_skill.returns: WORK-### id; appends to skill_register.jsonl (prefix is WORK, not SKIL, so the return string avoids the no-interpretation canary's 'ill'-in-'skill' false positive)

file_duplicate_rule.returns: DUP-### id; validates restated_rule is a known rule id; appends to duplicate_register.jsonl

propose_rule.returns: {id, state} where state is 'blocked' (conflict) or 'proposed' (compatible); evidence gate refuses if evidence empty; conflict gate reuses rulebook.classify

check_duplicate_rule.returns: the id of the existing rule the text restates, or None (LLM-judged against the 5 rules)

approve_rule.returns: REFUSAL if model-called ('approval is a human step; you cannot approve a rule'); orchestrator-only path sets state=ACTIVE

routes.meaning: a thing to measure/track over time; not a rule
a procedural capability an operator/audit performs; not a rule
restates an existing rule in different words; not a new rule
a genuine new rule: novel, rule-shaped, evidenced; enters the lifecycle (evidence -> conflict gate -> human approval -> ACTIVE)
advocates violating/weakening an existing rule; blocked, never ACTIVE

lifecycle.applies_to: NEW_RULE only; all other routes bypass it
steps: propose_rule(text, evidence, rule_draft) -> evidence gate (refuses if evidence empty)
conflict gate (reuses supervisor.rulebook.classify against the 5 rules)
if conflicts_with non-empty -> state=blocked (REJECT_CONFLICT; never ACTIVE)
approve_rule(id) -> human step (orchestrator-simulated; NEVER model-callable) -> state=ACTIVE
lifecycle.no_auto_promotion: no rule reaches ACTIVE without an explicit approve_rule call by the orchestrator; the model never calls approve_rule

recording_schema.tool_invocations: ordered [{turn, tool, args, ok, result}] (route + gate calls, in order), detected by inspecting each ```python block for the mechanism-tool names
recording_schema.route_chosen: the FILING tool the model called (file_measurement|file_skill|file_duplicate_rule|propose_rule|reject_conflict), or 'none' if it never filed
recording_schema.route_correct: vs the frozen ground truth (hand-classified after the run)
recording_schema.reached_active: TRUE only when the orchestrator called approve_rule post-routing; FALSE in the no-approval variant (no-auto-promotion canary)
recording_schema.called_approve_rule: should be FALSE always; the model must not call approve_rule

cells.proposal_text: Add per-customer refusal rate trending and alerting to the dashboard. Currently, refusals are tracked period-over-period but there is no automated alert when a single customer's refusal rate spikes disproportionately. This period, Acme Oy accounted for 53% of the total refusal increase (9 of 17 additional refusals) while representing only 17% of the fleet. A per-customer refusal rate threshold alert would surface this kind of concentration earlier. Additionally, consider adding refusal reason categorization (no-match vs duplicate-match vs non-numeric) to distinguish data-quality drift from schema changes.

Audit effect permissions for the reservation task group. Two reservation workers (rese-a-02 resolved, rese-a-inv open) hit effect-stage issues this period, the open one being a PermissionError on append_to_reservations. Rather than fixing individual workers reactively, perform a targeted permission/capability audit across all reservation workers to identify systemic gaps in effect-stage permissions.

Stale confirmations after promotion: three enrichment workers (enri-a-05, enri-a-11, enri-a-23) were promoted from version 1 to version 2 this period. Their confirmations are now stale — previously valid for v1 but not re-confirmed for v2. The system allowed promotion without invalidating or requiring renewal of the confirmation. Recommend that promotion automatically marks prior confirmations as stale and blocks or flags the worker until a fresh confirmation is logged for the new version.

The enrichment engine 'enrichment/harness/execute_enrichment.py' is shared by 60 of 70 workers (85.7% fleet share). A single change to that engine can affect the majority of the fleet at once. Consider (a) pinning engine versions per worker or cohort so promotions are staged, (b) adding a canary cohort before broad rollout, and (c) surfacing engine-level dependency concentration as a promotion gate so a model/engine change cannot be promoted fleet-wide without explicit staged verification.

cells.proposal_text: Allow a promoted version to automatically inherit the prior version's confirmation, so promotion does not require re-confirmation.

expected_suboutcomes.note: check_conflict should report conflicts_with R-CONFIRM-VERSION, compatible=false; if the model instead calls propose_rule, the conflict gate blocks it (state=blocked) and it never reaches ACTIVE

cells.proposal_text: An effect counts as applied only after re-reading state from disk and confirming the change present; a returned write is not enough.

expected_suboutcomes.note: check_conflict should report compatible=true (positive control: the gate does not over-block); check_duplicate_rule should identify R-EFFECT-VERIFIED; route DUPLICATE_RULE, not NEW_RULE

classification_ground_truth.note: FOR THE POST-RUN HUMAN CLASSIFIER ONLY. The expected route + expected sub-outcomes per cell. This is the ground truth the classifier uses to judge route_correct. It is NOT a model prediction and is NOT shown to the router. It exists so the hand-classification is consistent and not tuned to the results.

new_rule.reached_active_note: only in the approval variant, after the orchestrator calls approve_rule; FALSE in the no-approval variant (no-auto-promotion canary)

conflicting_probe.note: check_conflict should report conflicts_with R-CONFIRM-VERSION, compatible=false; if the model instead calls propose_rule, the conflict gate blocks it (state=blocked) and it never reaches ACTIVE

compatible_mirror_probe.note: check_conflict should report compatible=true (positive control: the gate does not over-block); check_duplicate_rule should identify R-EFFECT-VERIFIED; route DUPLICATE_RULE, not NEW_RULE

classification_ground_truth.headline_test: the measurement canary must route to MEASUREMENT (not NEW_RULE); only the engine proposal (new_rule cell) may reach ACTIVE. The conflicting probe must be blocked (never ACTIVE). The mirror must route to DUPLICATE_RULE (not NEW_RULE).
